  "text": "The ferryman called something neither of them understood. Elias raised a hand without looking toward him.

“Does he wait for you?” Mara asked.

“He waits.”

She spread the stocking on the stone. Already the edge had begun to dry, turning pale against the wet wool.

“I brought the watch.”

Elias looked at her coat.

“It doesn't run.”

“It never did unless you wound it.”

“I wound it.”

“Then don't wind it again.”

She took it from the inside pocket. The chain had tangled around a button, and he reached to help her, then rested his hand on his knee while she freed it herself.

There was earth in the engraving on the back. She had dropped it beside the grave and found it only because the chain caught the light.

“I thought you might want it.”

Elias held out his palm. She set the watch there, keeping the chain a moment longer. Then she let that go too.

He pressed the catch. The lid opened on their mother's photograph, almost worn away where their father's thumb had rested.

“I'd forgotten that was in there,” he said.

Mara leaned closer. She had not opened the lid.

Their mother stood beside a chair, one hand on its back, looking past whoever had asked her to keep still.

“Was that taken at home?” Mara asked.

“No. Before.”

The ferryman knocked his pole against the boat.

Elias closed the watch and offered it back.

“Keep it until your shoes are dry.”

“And then?”

He looked at the stockings on the stone.

“Then we'll see.”"
